name: Pedestrian Crossing
spec: fluorescent yellow-green diamond with a black walking-person symbol
meaning: Pedestrians may be crossing ahead; be ready to stop.

snippets.back: Fluorescent yellow on a sign marks pedestrian crossings and school zones.
The warning-sign examples identify intersections, signals, merges, wet-road skidding hazards, lane endings, schools, and pedestrian crossings.
Bicycle and pedestrian crossing signs are black symbols on yellow and mark places, such as a shared use path meeting a road, where both bicyclists and walkers may cross.
A HAWK beacon is a pedestrian crossing signal also called a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon.
Accessible pedestrian signals provide nonvisual crossing information through sounds, spoken messages or vibration.
A marked crosswalk can occur midblock as well as at an intersection, sometimes with a pedestrian signal at the crossing.
Pedestrian signals control only pedestrian movements and use the lighted words WALK and DON'T WALK together with the symbols of a walking person and an upraised palm.
A Pedestrian Crossing sign warns of crossing pedestrians who have the right of way and may require the driver to stop.

result.summary: Meaning supported by ID warning to stop for crossing pedestrians; spec supported by AL fluorescent yellow marking and CO black symbols on yellow for pedestrian crossing signs.
